title: Multi-timescale adaptive state for history-conditioned decision making
question: Does a compact multi-timescale persistent state improve exact task capability on history-dependent environments compared with no state and matched single-timescale state, at matched or explicitly accounted compute?
hypothesis: A multi-timescale adaptive state kernel will preserve decision-relevant temporal information across short, medium, and long regimes, improving held-out history-conditioned decisions while using bounded state/read/write computation.

endpoints.name: exact_class_balanced_success
endpoints.description: Exact generated task success, class-balanced, evaluated on untouched test episodes.

endpoints.name: history_conditioned_action_gap
endpoints.description: Absolute difference in action selection on paired histories with identical current observations but different optimal actions.

endpoints.name: adaptation_regret
endpoints.description: Cumulative regret after registered regime transitions.

endpoints.name: total_computation_work
endpoints.description: Total measured work including state read/write, routing, execution and verification; no dominant term may be omitted.

endpoints.name: persistent_state_footprint
endpoints.description: Number of active state elements attributable to persistent state.

decision_rule.condition: The primary endpoint improves materially for mtsk over both no_state and single_timescale, with the registered seed-level confidence interval excluding zero for the MTSK-vs-single-timescale contrast.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that the registered multi-timescale state mechanism improves exact history-conditioned capability on the finite benchmark under the registered compute accounting.
decision_rule.does_not_license: general intelligence, biological equivalence, asymptotic scaling, or cross-domain competence.

decision_rule.condition: MTSK improves history-conditioned action gap diagnostics but not exact class-balanced success.
decision_rule.licenses: the state changes history-dependent behavior but has not been shown to improve the registered capability endpoint.

decision_rule.condition: MTSK matches or loses to the matched single-timescale state.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered multi-timescale advantage is not supported on this benchmark.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of persistent state generally, failure of scale-free memory generally, or failure on other environments.

held_constant: parameter budget within preregistered matching tolerance
